blocks.text: Turkey and Greece work particularly well in the same trip. You can start among the mosques, palaces, and busy streets of Istanbul, spend a few days in Cappadocia, and then find yourself in Athens or on a Greek island later in the journey. The two countries are close, but the experience on each side of the Aegean is noticeably different.

Our Turkey and Greece Tours range from 8 to 18 days. Routes vary, but many combine Istanbul and Cappadocia with Athens, Santorini, or Mykonos. Longer itineraries can add Ephesus, Pamukkale, Crete, or more time on the Greek islands.

Depending on the tour, arrangements may include hotels with breakfast, guided sightseeing with licensed local guides, airport and port transfers, entrance fees, domestic flights within Turkey, and flights or seasonal ferries between Turkey and Greece. Private Tours, Small Group Tours, and Customized Tours are available across selected itineraries.

sections.heading: Turkey & Greece Tours at a Glance
Why Turkey and Greece Work Well Together

blocks.text: You do not need to choose between a cultural trip and time by the sea. Turkey gives you Istanbul, Cappadocia, archaeological sites, and very different landscapes within one country. Greece changes the pace, with Athens followed by island stays and more free time built into many itineraries.

There is also a practical reason to combine them. Istanbul and Athens are connected by direct flights, while seasonal ferries can link parts of Turkey's Aegean coast with nearby Greek islands. That makes it possible to build a two-country route without losing several days simply getting from one place to another.

sections.heading: How the Journey Usually Fits Together

blocks.text: There is no single Turkey and Greece itinerary, but most trips follow a natural geographical order.
In Turkey, Istanbul and Cappadocia form the core of many shorter programs. With additional time, Ephesus and Pamukkale can be added before crossing into Greece.

Athens is usually the first stop on the Greek side. From there, the trip can continue to Santorini or Mykonos, or both when the schedule allows. Longer tours may include another island or additional mainland sightseeing.

The important part is leaving enough time in each place. Adding Santorini and Mykonos to the same itinerary makes sense when there are enough days to enjoy them; on a shorter trip, one island can be the better choice.

sections.heading: How Many Days Do You Need?

blocks.text: With 8 to 10 days, it is better to keep the route focused. Istanbul, Cappadocia, Athens, and one additional stop can give you a good introduction to both countries without changing hotels every night.

At 11 to 14 days, there is more room to add Ephesus or Pamukkale in Turkey and spend time on Santorini and Mykonos in Greece. Our 10-Day Turkey & Greece Tour and 14-Day Best of Turkey & Greece Tour show two different ways of building the route.

With 15 to 18 days, the itinerary can slow down or cover more ground. Instead of simply adding stops, the extra days can be used for longer island stays, additional regions, or less travel between consecutive sightseeing days. See our 18-Day Turkey & Greece Tour for one of the longer options.

sections.heading: Flights or Ferries Between Turkey and Greece?

blocks.text: It depends on the route.

Flying between Istanbul and Athens is usually the straightforward choice when the Turkey portion finishes away from the Aegean coast. On other itineraries, a seasonal ferry connection may make more sense, particularly when the route moves from western Turkey toward the Greek islands.
Some trips also combine land touring with a Greek Islands cruise. Our 11-Day Greece Cruise & Turkey Land Tour is built around this type of journey.
The exact transportation is shown in each itinerary, so you can see where flights, ferries, transfers, and overland travel are used before choosing a tour.

May, June, September, and early October are particularly useful months for a trip covering both countries. The weather generally works well for sightseeing in Turkey while ferry services and island stays are operating normally in Greece.

July and August are busier and hotter, especially around archaeological sites and the Greek islands. They can still work well if island and coastal time are a priority, but travelers who prefer milder sightseeing conditions may find late spring or early autumn more comfortable.

sections.heading: Choosing the Right Turkey & Greece Tour

blocks.text: Start with the places you would be disappointed to miss.

If Istanbul, Cappadocia, Athens, and Santorini are your priorities, build the trip around those first. Add Ephesus, Pamukkale, Mykonos, or another island when the number of days genuinely allows it. A longer list of destinations does not necessarily make a better Turkey and Greece vacation.

Private Tours give you more control over sightseeing and timing, while Small Group Tours follow established departures and shared touring on selected parts of the itinerary. If an existing route is close to what you want, a Customized Tour can adjust the dates, hotels, number of nights, or overall pace.
Already decided to spend your whole trip in one country? Browse our Turkey Tour Packages or Greece Tour Packages. For journeys that continue beyond these two countries, see our Multi Country Tours.

faqs.q: How many days do you need for Turkey and Greece?
faqs.a: Our Turkey and Greece tours range from 8 to 18 days. An 8–10-day itinerary works best with a focused route, such as Istanbul and Athens, with Cappadocia or one Greek island added when travel connections allow. With 11–14 days, you can explore more of Turkey and spend time on one or two Greek islands. A 15–18-day itinerary allows for additional destinations or a more relaxed pace.

faqs.q: What is the best Turkey and Greece itinerary for first-time visitors?
faqs.a: A first-time Turkey and Greece itinerary should include Istanbul, Cappadocia, Athens, Santorini, and Mykonos or Crete. A 12 to 15-day route offers a strong mix of history, culture, landscapes, and island relaxation. The itinerary can also include Ephesus, Pamukkale, or additional Greek islands.

faqs.q: How much does a Turkey and Greece tour cost?
faqs.a: The cost of a Turkey and Greece tour depends on trip length, hotel category, travel season, included flights, ferry tickets, and whether the tour is private or small group. Mid-range packages usually cost less than luxury itineraries, while customized tours are priced according to your preferred services and destinations.

faqs.q: Is it better to visit Turkey or Greece first?
faqs.a: Both directions work well, but many travelers prefer starting in Turkey and continuing to Greece. This route allows you to explore Istanbul and Cappadocia before relaxing in Athens and the Greek islands. The best order depends on international flight schedules, ferry routes, seasonality, and your preferred arrival and departure cities.

faqs.q: What is the best month to visit Turkey and Greece?
faqs.a: May, June, September, and early October are among the best times to visit Turkey and Greece. These months usually offer pleasant weather, fewer crowds, and more comfortable sightseeing conditions. July and August are ideal for beaches but are also hotter, busier, and generally more expensive.

faqs.q: Are flights and ferries included?
faqs.a: Domestic flights and ferry tickets are often included when listed in the selected package itinerary. This may include flights within Turkey, international flights between Turkey and Greece, or ferries between Athens and the Greek islands. Exact inclusions vary, so travelers should always review the package details before booking.

faqs.q: Can Turkey and Greece tours be customized?
faqs.a: Yes. Turkey and Greece tours can be fully customized according to your travel dates, trip length, hotel preferences, budget, interests, and preferred pace. You can add or remove destinations, extend island stays, choose private services, upgrade hotels, and include special experiences such as balloon rides or private boat tours.

faqs.q: Are the tours private or small group?
faqs.a: Turkey and Greece combination tours can be arranged as private tours, small group tours, or a combination of both. Private services offer greater flexibility and personalized guiding, while small group options provide better value. Many travelers choose private sightseeing in major cities and shared tours in selected destinations.

faqs.q: Which Greek islands combine best with Turkey?
faqs.a: Santorini, Mykonos, Rhodes, Crete, Kos, and Samos combine well with Turkey, depending on your route and travel season. Santorini and Mykonos are ideal for first-time visitors, while Rhodes, Kos, and Samos are practical for travelers continuing from Turkey’s Aegean coast by ferry.

faqs.q: Do I need separate visas for Turkey and Greece?
faqs.a: Turkey and Greece have separate entry requirements. Greece follows Schengen visa rules, while Turkey has its own visa and entry system. Whether you need one or both visas depends on your nationality, passport type, and travel dates. Always check current official requirements before confirming your trip.

faqs.q: Is Cappadocia included in every itinerary?
faqs.a: Cappadocia is not included in every Turkey and Greece itinerary, but it is one of the most popular additions. It is especially recommended for first-time visitors who want to experience fairy chimneys, cave hotels, underground cities, and hot-air balloon flights. Shorter itineraries may focus only on Istanbul and Greece.

faqs.q: Can I add Egypt or Jordan to the tour?
faqs.a: Yes. Egypt or Jordan can be added to create a wider Multi Country Tour. Popular extensions include Cairo, the Pyramids, a Nile cruise, Petra, Wadi Rum, and Amman. Flights, hotels, transfers, licensed guides, and sightseeing can be coordinated within one customized itinerary managed by a single tour operator.

faqs.q: Which Greek islands are best for first-time visitors?
faqs.a: For first-time visitors, Santorini and Mykonos are the most popular choices. Santorini is famous for its dramatic caldera views, romantic sunsets, and volcanic scenery, while Mykonos offers beautiful beaches, charming whitewashed streets, and lively nightlife. Travelers with more time often add Crete, Rhodes, or Naxos for a more diverse Greek island experience.

faqs.q: Is Santorini worth visiting?
faqs.a: Absolutely. Santorini is widely regarded as one of the world's most beautiful islands, known for its cliffside villages, spectacular sunsets, luxury hotels, volcanic landscapes, and crystal-clear Aegean Sea views. It is an ideal destination for couples, honeymooners, photographers, and first-time visitors exploring Greece Tour Packages or multi-country Mediterranean itineraries.

faqs.q: Can I travel by ferry instead of flight?
faqs.a: Yes. Many Turkey and Greece Tours include scenic ferry journeys between the Greek islands, while international connections between Turkey and Greece usually operate by air for greater convenience. Depending on your itinerary, travel dates, and seasonal ferry schedules, we can recommend the most efficient combination of flights and ferries.

faqs.q: Which airports are used?
faqs.a: Airport selections depend on your itinerary. In Turkey, the most commonly used airports are Istanbul Airport (IST), Kayseri (ASR) or Nevşehir (NAV) for Cappadocia, and Izmir (ADB) for Ephesus. In Greece, travelers typically use Athens (ATH), Santorini (JTR), and Mykonos (JMK) airports for domestic and international connections.

faqs.q: What hotels are included?
faqs.a: Our tours include carefully selected 3-star, 4-star, and 5-star hotels, chosen for their quality, location, comfort, and guest reviews. Boutique hotels, cave hotels in Cappadocia, beachfront resorts, and luxury accommodations are available depending on the package. Every hotel is selected to provide excellent value and a comfortable travel experience.

faqs.q: Can I upgrade to luxury hotels?
faqs.a: Yes. All itineraries can be upgraded to premium accommodations, including luxury boutique hotels, internationally recognized five-star properties, cave suites in Cappadocia, and high-end resorts throughout Greece. Our travel specialists can recommend the best options based on your preferences, budget, and desired level of comfort.

faqs.q: Is travel insurance required?
faqs.a: Travel insurance is not mandatory for most travelers, but it is highly recommended. A comprehensive policy can provide valuable protection for unexpected medical expenses, trip cancellations, travel delays, lost baggage, and other unforeseen events, giving you greater peace of mind throughout your journey.

faqs.q: Can solo travelers join?
faqs.a: Yes. Solo travelers are welcome on both Small Group Tours and Private Tours. You may choose to share accommodation where available, request a private room for an additional supplement, or book a fully private itinerary. Our travel specialists will recommend the most suitable option based on your travel style and budget.
